title: Areopagus
name_variants: Ἄρειος Πάγος@grc | Areios Pagos | Areos Pagos | Ἄρειος Πάγος
description: Named after a mythical trial of the god Ares, the Areopagus is a rocky outcropping in Athens located to the northwest of the Acropolis. The hill was used as a meeting place for the Council of the Areopagus, which functioned as a council of elders for the city of Athens. The Areopagus is also traditionally identified as the setting for Paul's sermon to Athens.

title: Temple of Zeus Kasios
description: A temple at Pelusium, dedicated to the city's main deity, Zeus Kasios (identified with the Graeco-Egyptian Harpokrates). A set of inscriptions record that it was dedicated during the reign of Hadrian (117-138 AD). The archaeological remains are located approximately 200 metres west of the Late Roman fortress.

title: Roman theater at Vendeuil-Caply

title: Madrasa Gumushtakin

title: Ad Germani

It belonged to important senators like Sisenna Statilius Taurus and Calvia Crispinilla before its integration in the imperial property from the reign of Domitian (81 CE).

title: Gali͡ugaĭ
description: A Bronze Age settlement with burial mounds outside it, located in the modern the Terek River in Russia's Stavropol Krai. Scholars interpret this site as one of several defining the "Maykop culture", which flourished during the fourth millennium BCE in the western Caucasus.

title: House of the Golden Bracelet

title: Flaminio Obelisk (Rome)
description: The so-called "Flaminio Obelisk" at Rome was created in Egypt during the Nineteenth Dynasty under Pharaoh Seti I. The obelisk was erected at Heliopolis under Ramesses II. In 1 BCE, the obelisk was transported to Rome on the orders of Augustus. It was transported with the Obelisk of Montecitorio. The Flaminio Obelisk was re-erected on the spina of the Circus Maximus. It was discovered in a fragmentary state in 1587 along with the so-called Lateran Obelisk. Following the orders of Pope Sixtus V, Domenico Fontana restored the obelisk and erected it as the centerpiece of the Piazza del Popolo in 1589. It is supported by a travertine podium that was constituted from fragments of the Severan Septizodium on the flank of the Palatine Hill, a monument that had been demolished on papal orders.

title: Palatinus Mons
name_variants: Palatinus@la | Monte Palatino@it | Παλάτιον@grc | Palatine Hill@en | Palatinus | Monte Palatino | Palation | Palatine Hill | Παλάτιον | Palatinus
description: The central hill of Rome, Italy. Legend held that Romulus founded the city of Rome on the Palatine Hill following an augural contest with Remus, his brother.

title: Bizye Roman amphitheater
description: A Roman amphitheater in eastern Thrace.

title: Samshvilde
description: Fortified settlement in southern Georgia. The Samshvilde site is one of the oldest cities in Georgia, with remains from the Bronze Age Kura-Araxes Culture. Samshvilde was an important city in the late antique and medieval periods until it was sacked in 1440 by Jahan Shah; it went in decline but was inhabited as late as the 18th-19th centuries. The site includes a number of structures, including an 11th-13th century citadel, several early medieval churches, homes, and burial grounds.

title: Tolfa
description: The modern Italian comune of Tolfa is 24 kilometers northeast of Cerveteri. Its environs contain several ancient sites, dating from prehistory as well as the time of the Roman Empire.

title: Porta Santo Spirito
description: The Porta Santo Spirito is a gate of the Leonine Wall.

title: Villa El Soldán (The Sultan)
description: A Roman villa 300 meters east northeast of the eastern tip of Laguna Cernea, north of the modern village Santa Colomba de Somoza. Constructed under Tiberius, it was likely the residence of the official in charge of gold extraction.

title: el-Amrah

description: Predynastic and Early Dynastic burial site containing over 1,000 burials. It is the type-site of the Amratian culture.

title: Kupinovik Roman Villa
description: A Roman villa site on the modern Croatian island of Hvar (ancient Pharus).

title: Dur-Abiesuh
description: City founded by Babylonian king Abiesuh in the 18th-17th centuries. The location of this city is unknown, as cuneiform tablets from the site were taken in the 1990s without recording the location, but it is likely less than 50 km from Nippur.

title: Tomb of Aulus Umbricius Scaurus
name_variants: Tomb of Aulus Umbricius Scaurus@en | Tomb of Aulus Umbricius Scaurus
description: A tomb at Pompeii's Herculaneum gate that may be that of Aulus Umbricius Scaurus.

title: Great Bulmore
name_variants: Great Bulmore Roman settlement@en | Great Bulmore Roman settlement
description: Site of a suburban Roman settlement on the bank of the river Usk, 2 km. north-east of the legionary fortress at Caerleon.

title: Bona Dea
name_variants: Sacello della Bona Dea a Trastevere@it | Sacello della Bona Dea a Trastevere
description: A sanctuary of the Bona Dea is known to have existed in Rome's Trastevere district. The sanctuary was likely located just to the north of the Christian church of Santa Cecilia, and several inscriptions that record patronage directed to the sanctuary are known. This includes the benefactions of M. Vettius Bolanus.

title: mansio, via Tiburtina
description: A mansio located at the seventh mile of the Via Tiburtina.

title: Icknield Street
description: Icknield Street was a road of Roman Britain running from Fosse Way to Templeborough.

title: Metchley Fort
description: A Roman fort built in the area of modern Birmingham, England, soon after the Roman invasion of A.D. 43. The fort, about 200 square meters in area, was in use periodically until its abandonment ca. A.D. 120.

title: Su Coddu
name_variants: Su Coddu Eneolithic village@en | Su Coddu Eneolithic village
description: A prehistoric settlement covering some 10 hectares with evidence for approximately 150 huts located in Selargius, Sardinia.

title: Suburban Baths
description: A first century BC bath complex in Pompeii built against the walls near the Porta Marina

title: Merton Roman Camp
description: The so-called Merton Roman Camp was the site of a Roman parade ground and part of a temporary marching camp located 500m southeast of the Roman settlement of Alchester.

title: Monte Stallone catacomb (Formello)
name_variants: catacomba di Monte Stallone@it | catacomba di Monte Stallone
description: A Christian catacomb at Monte Stallone near Formello (Italy) was discovered in the 1960s.

title: Dover Castle
description: The twelfth-century medieval castle of Dover, England, sits atop earlier Roman fortifications.

title: Cavalupo Necropolis (Vulci)
description: Excavated in the nineteenth century and only recently re-assessed, this cemetery is located east of Vulci itself, across the modern river Fiora from the ancient acropolis. The cemetery was in active use from the Villanovan period through Hellenistic times.

title: Pompeion
description: A building between the Dipylon Gate and the Sacred Gate used for preparing the Panathenaic procession during the Classical and Hellenistic periods, destroyed during the Sullan Sack in 86 B.C., restored ca. A.D. 144, and destroyed again in the Herulian Sack of A.D. 267.

title: Laqê
details: In the 9th century B.C., Lāqê was annexed into Assyria and became part of the province of Raṣappa.
description: A land situated on the middle Euphrates, to north and west of the kingdom of Suhu and to the south of the land Bit-Halupê. Eleven of its cities are mentioned in Assyrian inscriptions of the first millennium B.C.

title: Second Temple, Jerusalem
description: The so-called "Second Temple" in Jerusalem stood on the northern edge of the Dome of the Rock and was destroyed in A.D. 70 during the Roman siege.

title: Basilica of St. Titus
description: A Christian basilica of the mid-sixth to seventh centuries.

title: Laphystios (Mountain)

title: Çemka Höyük
description: Çemka Höyük is a Pre-Pottery Neolithic site located in Mardin, Türkiye, dating to the tenth millennium BCE.

title: Cabu Abbas
description: A nuragic complex near Olbia, in the province of Sassari.

title: Wimblington
description: The site of a Romano-British settlement located in Wimblington, Cambridgeshire, England.

title: Ad Silma
description: Ad Silma was a place in Africa Proconsularis that is included on the Tabula Peutingeriana. It was located approximately 12 miles (ca. 18 km) northeast of Bulla Regia.

title: Llanfor

title: Vatican necropolis
description: The Vatican necropolis lies beneath Vatican City, specifically beneath the present St. Peter's Basilica, at depths ranging from 5 to 12 meters. The necropolis was partially exposed by means of archaeological excavations in 1940-1949. The necropolis was an open-air burial ground that included both mausolea and tombs. Notable among the documented tombs are the Tomb of the Iulii and the tomb that is conventionally believed to be that of Saint Peter (a.k.a. Peter the Apostle). The tomb of the saint, said to be located near the site of his martyrdom, provides a point of topographic orientation for the Constantinian project that came to be Old St. Peter's. The necropolis remained in use until at least 318.

title: Casa della Farnesina
description: An opulent Roman domus in the Transtiberim with a complex plan and an extraordinary program of painted and stuccoed decorations, the so-called "Casa della Farnesina" lies beneath the gardens of the Renaissance Villa della Farnesina. One hypothesis holds that it was built following the wedding of Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa and Iulia the Elder. Its wall paintings are a key example of the so-called 'Third style' of Roman wall painting.

title: Casiana
description: A fortress (phrourion) and settlement near Apamea on the Orontes river. The precise location is unknown today.

title: Potto Codinu necropolis

title: Roman Forum at Thugga
description: The Roman Forum at Thugga is large, covering more than 900 square meters.

title: Old Burrow

title: Alverdiscott

title: Clovelly Dykes

title: Thermopolium of Vetutius Placidus
name_variants: Thermopolium di Vetutius Placidus@it | Thermopolium of Vetutius Placidus@en | Thermopolium di Vetutius Placidus | Thermopolium of Vetutius Placidus

title: Eulmaš

Nabonidus claims to have rebuilt the temple on the original Sardonic Period foundations.

title: Theater at Segobriga

title: Volcanal

title: Comitium of Pompeii

title: Mont Vully oppidum

title: Moab (kingdom)

title: area Apollonis et Splenis et Calles

title: Mithraeum of the Seven Spheres
name_variants: Mitreo delle Sette Sfere@it | Mithraeum of the Seven Spheres@en | Mitreo delle Sette Sfere | Mithraeum of the Seven Spheres
details: Rodolfo Lanciani excavated the Mithraeum of the Seven Spheres in 1886. He discovered the building's foundation courses and mosaic pavements. On the basis of the brickwork technique, the shrine was dated to the Antonine period. The superstructure evident today is modern, built in order to protect the mosaic floors.
description: The so-called Mithraeum of the Seven Spheres is located in ancient Ostia near to the theater-cum-quadriporticus complex. The so-called Quattro tempietti screen it from the Decumanus Maximus.

title: Murgecchia
description: A place located in the territory of Matera that produced an ancient coin struck at Poseidonia and rediscovered in 1917.

title: Canneto sul Trigno

description: The remains of a Roman "Villa rustica" located adjacent to the Sanctuary of the Madonna di Canneto.

title: House of Venus in the shell

title: S. Passera hypogeum
description: A hypogeum connected with the S. Passera complex.

title: Sanctuary of the Dioscouri at Athens
description: Also known as the Anakeion, located likely East of the Acropolis.

title: House of Simon the Shoemaker
name_variants: House of Simon the Cobbler@en | House of Simon the Shoemaker@en | House of Simon the Cobbler | House of Simon the Shoemaker
description: A house at the southwestern corner of the Athenian Agora, built ca. 500 BC, destroyed during the Persian Sack in 480 BC, rebuilt in the 470s and demolished in the late fourth century BC. Finds suggest that in the third quarter of the fifth century BC it belonged to a shoemaker named Simon, perhaps to be identified with the interlocutor of Sokrates known from literary sources.

title: Arco Romano de Dona Isabel
name_variants: Arco Romano de Dona Isabel@pt | Arco Romano de Dona Isabel
description: The so-called "Arco Romano de Dona Isabel" is a second or third century A.D. city gate of Évora, the ancient site of Ebora Liberalitas Iulia.

title: Yarim Tepe (Iran)
description: Yarim Tepe was the site of a Neolithic settlement located in Iran's Gorgan plain. Archaeological fieldwork was first undertaken by V. E. Crawford in 1963.

title: Cryptoporticus (Alife)
description: An aisled Cryptoporticus at Alife that dates to the Augustan period.

title: Ecclesiasterion (Odeion) at Messene
name_variants: Odeion of Ancient Messene@en | Ecclesiasterion of Ancient Messene@en | Το Εκκλησιαστήριο (Ωδείο)@el | Odeion of Ancient Messene | Ecclesiasterion of Ancient Messene | To Ekklisiastirio (Odeio)

description: The Ecclesiasterion (Odeion) at Messene was originally constructed in the third century BCE and may be a converted ecclesiasterio/bouleuterion.

title: Roman theater at Carsulae
description: The Roman theater at Carsulae dates to the Augustan period, pre-dating the amphitheater.

title: House of the Surgeon (Rimini)

description: The so-called House of the Surgeon in Rimini may have been the home of a Roman doctor by the name of Eutyches.

title: Dólmenes de Antequera

description: A chamber tomb of the late second to early first millennium BCE located on the island of Minorca.

title: Theater at Alinda/Alexandria ad Latmum
description: The Roman Theater at Alinda could accommodate about 5,000 spectators.

title: Temple of Heracles
name_variants: Temple of Heracles@en | Temple of Hercules@en | Tempio di Eracle@it | Tempio di Ercole@it | Temple of Heracles | Temple of Hercules | Tempio di Eracle | Tempio di Ercole
details: The Temple of Heracles was constructed sometime in the late sixth or early fifth centuries BCE, in the Valley of the Temples, to the east of the primary city gate of ancient Akragas, sometimes known as Agrigentum. It is the second-largest temple at Akragas, measuring 67 by 25.34 meters. The temple is peripteral, with six columns in front and fifteen on each side, and the opisthodomos opens in the back. While there is no consensus on who built it, it was almost certainly one of the early fifth-century rulers of Akragas. Scholars such as Ross Holloway suggest Theron as the sponsor of the temple’s construction, but others such as Antony Spawforth indicate that the beginning of construction predates Theron’s rule. The temple is the earliest example of what would become a standard Sicilian temple. It contains the oldest known example of stairs, cut into the cella, leading to the roof. It is also the first example of angle contraction in temple corners. The temple at one point was said to have contained a painting by Zeuxis and a bronze statue of Heracles by Myron. The temple is referenced in Cicero’s In Verrem , where the orator claims Verres stole the statue of Heracles from the temple (2.4.94). There is evidence of a fire at the temple sometime in antiquity, and it had three small rooms added to it under Roman rule, one containing a statue of Asklepios.
description: The Temple of Heracles is one of the oldest temples in the Valley of the Temples in ancient Akragas, Sicily, dating from around the late 6th century BCE.

description: The so-called Villa di Grotte di Piastra, ruins of a Roman villa at Castelporziano.

title: Kalhu Archive 3
details: This archive is located in Fort Shalmaneser. Plan 67 . Kalhu . Plan of Fort Shalmaneser with archives Kalhu 1–5. From M. E. L. Mallowan, NR (1966), folding VIII.
description: Three seventh-century-B.C. archives were excavated in Fort Shalmaneser, a building complex in the southeastern corner of the city Kalhu. The archive consists of twenty-seven tablets, most of which are sealed. These documents are concerned with the rab ēkalli’s work as manager. The sealed clay bulla were attached to wooden objects such as boxes or writing boards and secured with a string.

title: Kalhu Archive 4

description: The remains of three Roman temporary camps.

title: Beljaus
description: Founded from Chersonesus in the late fourth century B.C., Beljaus was a fortified agricultural settlement located near the mouth of Lake Donuzlav.

title: Palatial House at Rhodes
description: A building at the foot of the Acropolis at Rhodes that occupied an entire insula and contained luxurious reception rooms and a large bath suite

title: Lethe (mythological river)
description: Mythological river of forgetfulness in the underworld

title: Arcus Traiani (divi Traiani)
description: The Arcus Traiani (or Arcus divi Traiani) is included in the listing for Regio I in the Regionary Catalogues. The monument has been the subject of a good deal of speculation, although the ultimate conclusion is that it is now unlocated. Writing in LTUR, D. Palombi rejects earlier correlations with the so-called Arco di Druso. Lanciani suggested that this lost arch was the source of the Trajanic sculptural elements reused in the decoration of the Arch of Constantine at Rome.

title: Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta
name_variants: Basilica di Santa Maria Assunta (Torcello)@it | Basilica di Santa Maria Assunta (Torcello)
description: The Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta on the island of Torcello is a Roman Catholic basilica initially founded in 639. The second basilica was begun in 1008.

title: Tell Qarqur
name_variants: تل قرقور‎‎@ar | Qarqaru@akk | Tell Qarqur | Qarqaru | Qarqara | Qarqari
description: A major settlement mound along the Orontes river in Syria with over 10,000 years of occupational history from the Pre-Pottery Neolithic to the Mamluk period.

title: Tholos at the Sanctuary of Asklepios, Epidauros
name_variants: Tholos at the Sanctuary of Asklepios@en | Θόλος@grc | Tholos at the Sanctuary of Asklepios | Epidaurus | Tholos | Θόλος
details: The Tholos at the Sanctuary of Asklepios in Epidaurus, designed by the architect Polykleitos the Younger, was constructed between 365-360 BCE and was finished 27 years later. The circular Tholos features a Doric architectural style with 26 columns surrounding the cella and 14 Corinthian columns inside the structure. Beneath the marble floor of the Tholos lies a constructed labyrinth. Although the purpose of this feature is unknown, it is theorized that it could have served as a dwelling for snakes, and emblems of Asklepios, or could have been used for healing or burial rites. In Pausanias, the structure is described as having paintings by Pausias depicting Love and Drunkenness, along with slabs written in Doric Greek inscribed with the names of those healed at the Sanctuary, the illnesses from which they suffered, and the treatment they received.
description: The Tholos, a circular structure in the Sanctuary of Asklepios at Epidaurus, was constructed between 365 and 360 BCE. Polykleitos the Younger designed it, and it features Doric architecture and a constructed labyrinth beneath its floor.

title: Xocalı
name_variants: Խոջալու@hy | Xocalı@az-Latn | Khojalu | Chodshali | Khojaly | Xocalı
description: Extensive groups of Iron Age tumuli in the Lesser Caucasian mountains. A Neo-Assyrian seal bearing the name of Adad-nirari II (911-891 BCE) was found here during excavations in 1895.

title: Kástron Khóstion
name_variants: Κάστρον Χώστιον@el | Πρόδρομος@el | Χώστια@el | Ακρόπολη Κορσιών στα Χώστια (Πρόδρομος)@el | Kastron Khostion | Kástron Khóstion | Prodromos | Pródromos | Pródhromos | Khostia | Khóstia | Chostia | Akrópoli Korsión sta Chóstia (Pródromos) | Akropoli Korsion sta Khostia | Akropole Korison sta Chostia
details: The site is often referred to as Khóstia, the former name of the nearby modern settlement now known as Pródhromos.
description: A complex of structures dating to the Greek and Roman period, with ceramic evidence of prior occupation of the vicinity, on a spur of Palióvouno, overlooking a valley leading to the bay of Saránda on the Korinthian Gulf. The excavators associate this site with the attested classical city of Khorsiai on the basis of epigraphic evidence recovered at the site.

title: Tall Karay Qāsim
name_variants: تل گري قاسم@ar | Tall Karay Qāsim
description: Small mound, periodically submerged in water, where cuneiform inscription has been found.

title: Ābādān (island)
name_variants: جزیره آبادان@fa | جزيرة عبادان@ar | Abadan Island@en | Jazireh Abadan | Jazirat Eibadan | Abadan Island
description: An island in modern Iran at the head of the Persian Gulf, bounded today on the southwest by the Shatt al-Arab and on the northeast by the Bahmanshir. Its name first appears certainly in 9th century CE sources, but it may relate to an apparent cognate preserved in Ptolemy and its general topography (or that of an earlier island in the vicinity) may have been known to some Greek and Roman geographers.

title: Qasr el-Sagha temple
name_variants: قصر الصاغة@arz | Qasr al-Ṣagha | Qasr el-Ṣagha
description: Temple located north of Lake Qarun in the Fayyum Depression. Tentatively dated to the Old Kingdom period, the temple may have been dedicated to the god Sobek.

title: Temple of Kalabsha
description: An ancient temple dated ca. 30 BCE was originally located at Bab al-Kalabsha (Gate of Kalabsha), some 50 km south of Aswan. It was relocated to its present site during the construction of the Aswan High Dam with sponsorship from the government of Germany.

title: Castle of Dokos
description: The Castle of Dokos located on the Dokos islet was founded in the seventh century CE.

title: Puig de Castellet
description: A pre-Roman oppidum located in the municipality of Lloret de Mar and occupied by the Ausetani. The site was short-lived and abandoned after the Roman conquest.

title: Eanna
description: The temple of the god Anu and the goddess Ištar at Uruk. The Sumerian ceremonial name Eanna means "House of Heaven."

title: Homarium
description: The Homarium (ca. 371 BCE) served as the common sanctuary of the Achaean League.

title: Chanctonbury Ring
description: Chanctonbury Ring is a prehistoric hill fort located on Chanctonbury Hill in West Sussex, England. It is part of the present-day South Downs Way.

title: Tsarëv Kurgan
name_variants: Цaрев курган@ru | Tsarëv kurgan | Tsarev kurgan | Tsaryov kurgan
description: A funerary mound on the bank of the Volga River in Samara Oblast', Russia, south of Volzhskiy.

title: Dikili Tash
description: Dikili Tash is a prehistoric tell in eastern Macedonia, approximately 1.5 km east of ancient Philippi. The site has been excavated by the École française d’Athènes in stages since 1920. Neolithic and Bronze Age deposits have been investigated.

title: Roman amphitheater at Bern
description: The remains of a small Roman amphitheater at Bern, measuring ca. 27.5 x 25.3 meters, are visible on satellite images.

title: Temple d'Appolon
description: The ruins of a Roman-period temple dedicated to Apollo located at the Oppidum de Gaujac (Gard, France).

title: Göreme National Park and the Rock Sites of Cappadocia
description: A natural erosional landscape within which a number of rupestral sanctuaries are located, dating as early as the fourth century A.D.

title: Khirbet al-Batrawy
description: Settlement near the modern city of Zarqa in Jordan, inhabited during the Early Bronze Age (ca. 3000-2000 BCE).

title: Maltepe (Pergamon)
description: The Maltepe tumulus at Pergamon is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Pergamon and its Multi-Layered Cultural Landscape".

title: Ad Palmam
description: Ad Palmam was a place in North Africa and is included on the Peutinger map. It is located along the route from a place called Lacene, also unlocated, to Tacape.

title: Til-karme
details: Til-karme is an unlocated city in Gurgum. It has been suggested that it was located east of the Amanus Mountains, on the border with Bīt-Agūsi.
description: Til-karme is a city in Gurgum that is mentioned in an inscription of the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser III (r. 744-727 BC).

title: Paqarhubuni (settlement)
name_variants: Paqirahubuna@akk | Paqarruhbuni@akk | Paqarhubni@akk | Paqirahubuna | Paqirahupuna | Paqarruhbuni | Paqarruhpuni | Paqarhubni | Paqarhupni
details: The location of the city Paqarhubuni is uncertain. Some scholars place Paqarhubuni to the north of modern Gaziantep, while others suggest that it was south of that modern location. The Helsinki Atlas tentatively identifies Paqarhubuni as Gaziantep (certainty "3" = "uncertain"). Alternatively, it has been suggested that Paqarhubuni was located in the vicinity of Pazarcık since a stele of the Assyrian king Adad-nērārī III (r. 809-782 BC) mentioning the city Paqarhubuni was discovered in a nearby village ( Kızkapanlı ) during the construction of a dam.
description: Paqarhubuni is a city that was part of Bīt-Adini during the reign of the Assyrian king Shalmaneser III (r. 858-824 BC); it might have been part of Bīt-Agūsi while Adad-nērārī (r. 809-782 BC) was king of Assyria. The city and its surrounding region were between the kingdoms of Gurgum and Kummuhu.

title: Roman amphitheater at Eporedia
description: The extramural Roman amphitheater at Eporedia is evidence of the expanding suburbium of the Roman settlement.

title: Boville Ernica
description: A hilltop settlement with megalithic fortifications.

title: Alto Chacón, Teruel
description: An Ibero-Roman oppidum located just west of modern Teruel in Spain.

title: Tel Mor
name_variants: תל מור@he | Tel Mor | Tell Mor
description: Archaeological site on the northern bank of the Lachish River with signs of habitation dated from the Late Bronze Age to the Hellenistic period.

title: Sep. Scipionum
name_variants: hypogaeum Scipionum@la | sepolcro degli Scipioni@it | tomb of the Scipios@en | hypogaeum Scipionum | sepolcro degli Scipioni | tomb of the Scipios | hypogaeum Scipionum
description: A family tomb of the Cornelii Scipiones near the Porta San Sebastiano in use from the third century B.C. to the first century A.D.

title: Statues of Harmodios and Aristogeiton
name_variants: Statues of Harmodios and Aristogeiton@en | Ἁρμόδιος καὶ Ἀριστογείτων@grc | Statues of Harmodios and Aristogeiton | Harmódios kaì Aristogeítōn | Ἁρμόδιος καὶ Ἀριστογείτων
description: Statues of the tyrannicides Harmodios and Aristogeiton, the assassins of the tyrant Hipparchos and symbols of the Athenian democracy. An initial pair, made by Antenor were erected in the Athenian Agora ca. 510 BC, taken away to Susa by the Persians in 480 BC and returned by Alexander or one of his successors in the late fourth century BC. A replacement pair, made by Kritios and Nesiotes were erected in the Athenian Agora in 477 BC. With few exceptions it was forbidden to erect other statues in the vicinity. Part of the base of the second pair has been found, but not in situ.

title: Gaochang
description: Gaochang is the site of an ancient oasis city located on the northern rim of the inhospitable Taklamakan Desert in present-day Xinjiang, China.

title: House of the Ceii
name_variants: House of L. Ceius Secundus@en | House of Fabia and Tyrannus@en | Casa dei Ceii@it | House of the Ceii@en | I.6.15@en | House of L. Ceius Secundus | House of Fabia and Tyrannus | Casa dei Ceii | House of the Ceii | I.6.15
details: The house was excavated in 1913 and 1914. The name L. Ceius Secundus is mentioned in a painted campaign message on the house's facade. The duovir L. Ceius Secundus was the presumed owner of the House of the Ceii.
description: A Roman house in Pompeii (I, 6, 15), also known as the House of L. Ceius Secundus. It is also referred to as the House of Fabia and Tyrannus.

title: House of the Lararium of Achilles
name_variants: Casa del Larario di Achille@it | House of the Lararium of Achilles@en | House of the Ilion Sanctuary@en | I.6.4@en | Casa del Larario di Achille | House of the Lararium of Achilles | House of the Ilion Sanctuary | I.6.4
description: The so-called "House of the Lararium of Achilles" (I ,6 ,4) lies on the Via dell'Abbondanza. Excavated in 1912 and 1913, it is also known as the "House of the Ilion Sanctuary".

title: Monte Tamburino necropolis
details: A necropolis located close to Monte Bibele where over 100 fourth century B.C. Etruscan tombs have been excavated.
description: A necropolis with inhumations dating to the fifth and fourth centuries B.C.

title: Tower of Vravrona
name_variants: tower of Vravrona@en | tower of Vravrona
description: A Frankish tower dating to the thirteenth century.

title: Circuit wall of Rusellae
name_variants: walls of Rusellae@en | Mura di Roselle@it | Stadtmauer von Roselle@de | walls of Rusellae | Mura di Roselle | Stadtmauer von Roselle
description: The megalithic defensive circuit of Rusellae dates to the seventh and sixth centuries B.C. and represents an important early example of stone-built fortifications in central Italy.

title: Alpes Graiae (province)
name_variants: Alpes Graiae@la | Graiae Alpes@la | Alpes Graiae | Graiae Alpes
description: A small Alpine province of the Roman Empire organized around the Little St Bernard Pass, roughly corresponding to the eastern portion of the modern-day French department of Savoie. Augustus annexed the territory in 15 BCE; under Diocletian, the periodically joint administration of the province together with Alpes Poeninae was made permanent, forming the province of Alpes Poeninae et Graiae.

title: Rudston Roman Villa
details: Barrington Atlas: Rudston seems to correspond to the center of the modern village but the villa is located west of it. This Place represents the villa proper.
description: A fourth-century CE Romano-British villa west of the modern village of Rudston.
